title: 'Flavortown' in WNC, restaurant previews, the ultimate chef cook-offs - NewsBreak
text:
By Tiana Kennell ,
12 hours ago Hello, and welcome back to another edition of AVL Bites and Brews!
This week, I am wondering if Asheville's new moniker could become "Flavortown?"
This comes after more episodes of "Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives" featuring Asheville and Black Mountain restaurants have been confirmed. The hit Food Network show is hosted by Guy Fieri, also known as the "Mayor of Flavortown," and it appears that he was hungry for all Western North Carolina has to offer during his visit to the area last December.
Episodes have been released for Season 43, which has included Huli Sue's BBQ & Grill, and stay tuned for Foothills Grange's episode, premiering this Friday on Food Network. Little Chango, which was recently in the headlines for receiving a Michelin Bib Gourmand award , will be featured on the show on March 13 ― and more undisclosed restaurants' episodes are to come. Read these stories for more details about what Fieri ate and loved at Huli Sue's and The Grange .
Another Asheville chef brought the heat to another Guy Fieri Food Network show last weekend. The James Beard Media Award-winning Ashleigh Shanti competed on “Tournament of Champions: The Qualifiers" for a spot on the bracket of the main event, kicking off on March 1. How did the Good Hot Fish owner perform? Read this story for a play-by-play of her cook-off challenge .
Then, on March 4, tune into CBS to watch Chef Katie Button, of the Michelin-recommended restaurant Cúrate , compete for $1 million on the new series, "America's Culinary Cup."
Many exciting moments have been happening off-screen, too, including the opening of Le Parisien and Rhubarb downtown.
What a treat to celebrate and enjoy dishes from the French-inspired and farm-to-table Appalachian restaurants, and to talk to the teams about their motivations, missions and menus.
Take a menu tour of Le Parisien , led by Paris native Chef Gabriel Attala.
And read the story about Chef John Fleer passing the torch to the new leaders of Rhubarb.

Food and Dining Reporter, Asheville Citizen Times
